| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [../specs/workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](../specs/seat-binding.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [../specs/seat-binding.md](../specs/seat-binding.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Identity (foundation; today the local session writer id) | Foundation authority for identities, today for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-identity` (`packages/identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs` over the combined addon's `sessionIdentity` namespace. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Also mints and reads the machine id (`<stateRoot>/machine-id`, optional `machine-alias`; `fgos identity machine`, doctor row `identity-machine-id`) and derives the machine handle; also reads and, on an explicit `fgos identity project --init`, mints the project id (the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`; doctor row `identity-project-id`; the provider reads the Git component for the trusted main root and the remote default branch); the one validator of the id shape lives here. The host provider sits behind the default cargo feature `provider` (needs `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-convention`, `fgos-git`); Event Store and the node addon depend on the library with `default-features = false`, so the event log never pulls the host runtime. The process-tree adapter reads `/proc` through `fgos-process` (a plain dependency, an L0 leaf, not behind `provider`). Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint and, through the library without `provider`, the ISO-8601 UTC clock `text::iso_utc_now` (host-runtime's `civil_time` stays the clock of the crates that already sit on the host runtime; it cannot call identity, whose provider depends on it). The machine-id mint reaches Node through the addon's `sessionIdentity.mintMachineId`, wrapped by `src/util/identity-mint.mjs`. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [identity/spec.md](identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one vector file run by cargo), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; Node reaches it only through the in-process door (`src/native/door.mjs` → `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`, six exports, at most 60 lines, no `/proc`, no `process.kill`); reconcile imports the thin client. Callers reclaim only on `dead` and count a process stopped only after a `sent` signal and a `dead` judgement; `unknown` always holds. Loader errors `process-door-unavailable` and `process-door-not-shipped` fail closed with a next step. No Node file judges a recorded process or signals a bare pid: the only `process.kill` calls left signal the process group of a child the same code just spawned, and the remaining `/proc` readers (lock-holder fd scan, doctor checks, confinement probes) are listed with their reasons in `test/process/one-door.test.mjs`, which fails on any other site. The doctor row kept is `process-containment`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank and path), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule and the single state-root resolution. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon, which the facade takes once through a one-shot capability (Node runs every lock operation in process on Linux and macOS), and the four surviving internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd` (borrowed check and shared try, for the git hook), `lock-hold` (Windows), `quiesce-scan` and `lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. The state root is the host's pin, else the door's `holderLock.stateRoot`; the checkout channel `node bin/fgos.mjs` is unsupported for lock verbs. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`); the file mode is explicit, and an omitted or invalid mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`) before anything is written. A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate and Rust consumers done, Node door not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, section schemas and standard done, not yet wired to any caller) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

## 5. How To Change

1. Read this anchor and the current detailed component-boundary source.
2. Identify whether the change is component packaging, bounded context, authority boundary, or physical layout.
3. Update the owning area docs.
4. Update this anchor or the detailed source when the whole-system map changes.
5. Link evidence or record `No component-boundary change`.

selected.text:
| Component | Current role | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [../specs/workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md), [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](../specs/seat-binding.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [../specs/seat-binding.md](../specs/seat-binding.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [../specs/runner.md](../specs/runner.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md](../specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [../specs/confinement-authority.md](../specs/confinement-authority.md) |
| Run Result Evaluator | Evidence/confidence boundary for assignment run results. | [../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md](../architect/agent-coordination/architecture/evidence-and-results.md) |
| Domain Components And Extension Layer | Domain-specific behavior, workflows, skills, task specs, doctrine. L2 prose no longer picks executors or mechanisms (lớp matching L2 cũ đã thu hồi per 0048); thin driver `fgos-run` delegates directly to the Workflow door (`fgos workflow start`) and P1 Execution Core (`fgos run`); a conductor names the Workflow case on each dispatch. | [../../domains/](../../domains/), [../architect/domainization/](../architect/domainization/) |
| Host And Surface Layer | CLI, fgos Gateway (REST/MCP/web), `herdr-dashboard` plugin and other Herdr surfaces into platform engines. | Host invocation and gateway docs |
| Packaging-Distribution | Runtime packaging, install, activation, setup/doctor readiness. | [packaging-distribution/README.md](packaging-distribution/README.md) |
| Knowledge, Learning, And Documentation Registry | Retrospective learning, doc registry, end-user docs index, trace/evolve signals. | Knowledge and docs registry docs |
| Observe (Metrics & Friction) | Measurement and friction tracking across substrate entities (cases, runs, sessions, friction, snapshots). Owned in Rust (`packages/observe/rust`), native routing. | [../specs/observe.md](../specs/observe.md) |
| Convention (Executable Names & Placement) | Platform-core authority for deterministic artifact names, repository-relative placement, path classification, and conformance checking. Implemented; owns no state and depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. | [convention/spec.md](convention/spec.md) |
| Identity (foundation; today the local session writer id) | Foundation authority for identities, today for "who is the writer of this process" (`{id, source}`). One implementation, the Rust crate `fgos-identity` (`packages/identity/rust`, native verb `fgos identity`); Observe calls it in process, Node through the facade `src/util/session-identity.mjs` over the combined addon's `sessionIdentity` namespace. Also mints the writer id of an attempt (`att-<attemptId>`) and carries the launcher's env scrub the gate applies. Also mints and reads the machine id (`<stateRoot>/machine-id`, optional `machine-alias`; `fgos identity machine`, doctor row `identity-machine-id`) and derives the machine handle; also reads and, on an explicit `fgos identity project --init`, mints the project id (the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`; doctor row `identity-project-id`; the provider reads the Git component for the trusted main root and the remote default branch); the one validator of the id shape lives here. The host provider sits behind the default cargo feature `provider` (needs `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-convention`, `fgos-git`); Event Store and the node addon depend on the library with `default-features = false`, so the event log never pulls the host runtime. The process-tree adapter reads `/proc` through `fgos-process` (a plain dependency, an L0 leaf, not behind `provider`). Observe depends on it; the run supervisor's controller half calls the mint and, through the library without `provider`, the ISO-8601 UTC clock `text::iso_utc_now` (host-runtime's `civil_time` stays the clock of the crates that already sit on the host runtime; it cannot call identity, whose provider depends on it). The machine-id mint reaches Node through the addon's `sessionIdentity.mintMachineId`, wrapped by `src/util/identity-mint.mjs`. Grants no lock or claim authority. | [identity/spec.md](identity/spec.md) |
| Terminal-control (L2) | Foundation component for "which pane does this key run in" on a terminal multiplexer, usable without a run. Rust crate `fgos-terminal-control` (`packages/terminal-control/rust`) with a key-addressed upper port and a driver port with declared capabilities (herdr first; Windows declares none). Writes only the allocation record; closes only panes it allocated, never a tab; Node reaches it through the internal route `fgos internal terminal-control`, no user verb. Dependency one way: run supervisor → Terminal-control (the supervisor holds the key, the attempt id, never a pane). Node migration done; setup adds the `terminal` config section and `<stateRoot>/terminal`, doctor runs `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations`. | [terminal-control/spec.md](terminal-control/spec.md) |
| Process Facts & Control (L0) | Single authority for "is this process tuple `{host, bootId, pidNs, pid, startTime}` alive, dead or unknown" (`judge`, one vector file run by cargo), for signalling a process by identity (`pidfd` on Linux, never a bare pid), for spawning with an explicit fd mapping, and for the domain primitives `domain_is_empty`/`domain_kill_all` the predecessor rule of holder-lock needs. Never spawns to read facts, never kills by bare pid, never reads mtime, knows no run, lock or pane. Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), one driver per OS; Node reaches it only through the in-process door (`src/native/door.mjs` → `src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`, six exports, at most 60 lines, no `/proc`, no `process.kill`); reconcile imports the thin client. Callers reclaim only on `dead` and count a process stopped only after a `sent` signal and a `dead` judgement; `unknown` always holds. Loader errors `process-door-unavailable` and `process-door-not-shipped` fail closed with a next step. No Node file judges a recorded process or signals a bare pid: the only `process.kill` calls left signal the process group of a child the same code just spawned, and the remaining `/proc` readers (lock-holder fd scan, doctor checks, confinement probes) are listed with their reasons in `test/process/one-door.test.mjs`, which fails on any other site. The doctor row kept is `process-containment`. The gate primitives (subreaper, PDEATHSIG, PID namespace, tty) stay with the run supervisor; the containment port lives in this crate (row below). Depends only on the OS. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md) |
| Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank and path), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule and the single state-root resolution. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the `holderLock` namespace of the combined addon, which the facade takes once through a one-shot capability (Node runs every lock operation in process on Linux and macOS), and the four surviving internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd` (borrowed check and shared try, for the git hook), `lock-hold` (Windows), `quiesce-scan` and `lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. The state root is the host's pin, else the door's `holderLock.stateRoot`; the checkout channel `node bin/fgos.mjs` is unsupported for lock verbs. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
| Containment port (L0) | Single authority for "which processes belong to this attempt, and are there any left": an OS-neutral process domain per attempt (`create`, `spawn_in`, `is_empty`, `kill_all`, `guarantee`) with one driver per OS (`bwrap-pidns` and `linux-pgroup` on Linux, `windows-job`, `macos-tree`), each reporting a guarantee level (`kernel` or `best-effort`) and its named escapes. Knows no attempt beyond the id that names a domain, and no envelope, lock or pane. Module `containment` of the Rust crate `fgos-process` (`packages/process/rust`), contract `packages/process/contracts/containment.port.v1.json`; depends only on the OS. The `linux-pgroup` driver sets no subreaper on its caller and answers `is_empty` `unknown`, never `empty`, when a seen or listed member cannot be judged or read. Node has no caller of `create`, `spawn_in`, `guarantee` or the domain calls, so the addon exports none of them. | [process/spec.md](process/spec.md#10-containment-port) |
| Durable file (L0 leaf) | Single authority for how an fgOS record reaches disk when its loss must not go unnoticed: temp file, fsync of the file, install (replace, or create-only without replacing), fsync of the directory; every error says the step it failed at and which effect already happened (`installed: created \| already-exists \| none`); the file mode is explicit, and an omitted or invalid mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`) before anything is written. A create-only writer that finds the name already there leaves without a directory fsync. Rust crate `fgos-durable-file` (`packages/durable-file/rust`); Node through the door exports `replaceDurably` and `installOnce` in `src/native/door.mjs`, which remove the retained temporary on failure. Node keeps its per-module no-fsync helpers (no shared write helper), each naming its temporary with `uniqueTmpTag()`; the mode-preserving trust store, copy-then-rename and Work-owned writes stay. Accepted duplication: the private temp-then-rename helpers of the run supervisor (`supervise.rs`, `adopt.rs`, `supervise/windows.rs`) and holder-lock (`route/hold.rs`, `predecessor.rs`) do not fsync, because a heartbeat fsync on every tick would add I/O to every live run. Node budget: the Node replace and create-only helpers that already fsynced are deleted (target Node −110). Depends only on the OS. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| Canonical JSON (L0 leaf) | Single authority for the bytes of canonical JSON: RFC 8785 member order by UTF-16 code units and ECMAScript number text; input that is not JSON is refused by name. Rust crate `fgos-canonical-json` (`packages/canonical-json/rust`, `canonical_json`, `canonical_line`), vectors in `packages/canonical-json/contracts/vectors/`; Node through the door export `canonicalJson(value)` (`src/native/door.mjs`), which serialises with `JSON.stringify` (so a `Date` becomes its `toJSON` text) and hands the text to Rust, and refuses a hole, a non-finite number or a value `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise with `canonical-json-not-json` and drops an `undefined` member as `JSON.stringify` does. Node budget: one re-export line. Accepted exceptions, each with its reason: `recovery-planner.mjs` keeps its own `stableStringify` (its module contract is purity, its import set is pinned to `node:crypto`, and its stored records hold only hash outputs); `effective-execution-contract.mjs` and the release-manifest producer and verifier pair stay together until the Packaging plan moves them as one; `trust-store.mjs` `sortedJson` stays because it must match codex's own byte order, not RFC 8785. Depends only on `serde_json` and `ryu-js`. | This row, until a spec of its own exists |
| YAML Document (L0 leaf; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate and Rust consumers done, Node door not started) | Single authority for reading, editing and merging YAML text: a lossless document with semantic value and positions, two parse profiles (`strict-config` for config files, `tool` for workflows, personas, units and manifests, the latter keeping today's js-yaml door contract), edits that keep every untouched byte, comment blocks as positioned text with an injection guard, and a merge primitive whose per-path rules the caller supplies. Knows no config key, file scope, default, lock or comment grammar. Rust crate `fgos-yaml-doc` (planned `packages/yaml-doc/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `yaml` behind the kept facade `src/util/yaml.mjs`; replaces the vendored js-yaml (RUL101 superseded when it lands); `frontmatter.mjs` and `distill.mjs` stay on their own paths. Depends only on its parser crate. | [yaml-document/spec.md](yaml-document/spec.md) |
| Config (L1; spec signed 2026-10-22; Rust crate, section schemas and standard done, not yet wired to any caller) | Single authority for fgOS configuration: which files are config (project `.fgos/config.yaml` over global `~/.fgos/config.yaml` over the read-only standard shipped with the release; config files hold only differences; account pools and the gateway token under `~/.fgos/private/`, hidden from confined workers), the schema dialect and engine (descriptors are data shipped by each section's owner under `core/config-schema/`), the effective snapshot with provenance, the three write doors (`init`, `doctor --fix`, `fgos config`) and their one-file transaction (new locks `project-config` and `global-config`, compare-and-swap on byte revision, Durable File replace), the `@fgos:doc` / `@fgos:why` comment grammar and when a reason is required, the config doctor checks and JSON-to-YAML migration. Reads never write. Never owns YAML syntax (YAML Document), lock mechanism (Holder-lock), secret values (Secrets), section meaning or cross-field rules (each section owner), or bootstrap JSON files. Rust crate `fgos-config` (planned `packages/config/rust`); Node through the native door namespace `config`, replacing `src/config/` and every direct reader. Depends on YAML Document, Holder-lock, Durable File and Secrets; acquires its own locks without reading config. | [config/spec.md](config/spec.md) |
| Git (foundation) | Single authority for repository facts, typed Git operations and their recovery WAL: every fgOS mutation of local objects, refs, index, worktrees and worktree registration, the local side of fetch and push, and operation recovery, through typed ports (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication); no public `git(args)` port. Its Publication port is the only door to `refs/fgos/*`, and Event Store is the only production writer of event refs through it. Owns no business approval, Work lifecycle, event semantics or lock mechanism. Consumers: Workflow, Execution Core, Work, Event Store, setup. Depends on Holder-lock, Process Facts & Control and Session Identity; imports no consumer. Rust crate `fgos-git` (`packages/git/rust`); Node reaches it only through the one combined N-API addon (`packages/git/node-addon`) that also links `fgos-event-store`, via the facade `src/git/`. Implemented through Git phase 07 (callers moved onto the typed ports); the whole-product one-door gate (`git-mutation-one-door`, spec §12) and the phase 08 proofs land with the Git plan's final release. | [git/spec.md](git/spec.md) |
| Event Store (foundation) | Single authority for how an fgOS event becomes durable, is sealed into git objects on per-machine `refs/fgos/*`, is shared across machines and is read back: the v4 envelope and stream registry, the per-stream open logs and their `event-append`/`event-seal` locks, seal and recovery, the reader with coverage, causal order and cursor, sync, and the store side of the `fgos events` verbs (`src/verbs/events/`). Planned consumers: Work, porting, observe, decisions; each owns its types, gate, reducer and view, and the store imports none of them (`packages/event-store/contracts/consumers.v1.json` is the only registry). Depends on Git's Publication port (the only door to `refs/fgos/*`), Holder-lock and Session Identity. Rust crate `fgos-event-store` (`packages/event-store/rust`); Node only through the facade `src/event-store/` over the one combined N-API addon shared with `fgos-git`. Dormant on main: store layer proven (2026-10-20), no consumer registered; the Work cutover is the WORK lane. | [event-store/spec.md](event-store/spec.md) |
| Run Supervisor (L4) | One Rust process per attempt that owns the attempt after the controller handed it over: holds the attempt lock and the cwd lease, creates the containment domain, starts the launch gate, watches the soft deadline and idle, publishes the receipt and the per-step receipts, runs the post-receipt steps and owns the adopt door (`fgos internal adopt`, one door for resume, recover, scan and home cleanup). A supervisor that dies leaves the agent running; adopt settles it. Never knows a pane or a terminal, never picks a provider or retries, never judges the work (Run Result Evaluator inside the Node `settle-attempt` step). Crate `fgos-run-supervisor` (`packages/run-supervisor/rust`), routes `fgos internal supervise\|gate\|adopt\|attempt-step` (protocol 1, not in help), Node client and steps in `src/run-supervisor/`. Depends on Containment port, Process Facts & Control, Holder-lock and agent-protocol. Two launch modes: `direct` (headless process) and `terminal` (an agent in a terminal-control pane, addressed by the attempt id; the supervisor listens on an attempt socket, drives the pane through the agent protocol and ends with a `release-slot` step). Depends also on Terminal-control (in process, by key). | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md) |
| Launch gate (L4, part of the run supervisor) | The process root of the agent inside the containment domain (pid 1 of a fresh PID namespace on Linux): owns the agent's IO (capture files, stdin; in `terminal` mode the pane's tty, with the agent as foreground group), refuses to run the agent without GO (in `terminal` mode GO arrives over the attempt socket with the attempt lock and cwd lease as `SCM_RIGHTS`, the peer uid is checked, and the gate runs in the pane, so the gate holds the attempt lock and outlives a dead supervisor), applies the environment scrub and the attempt writer id, reaps every orphan with `waitpid(-1)` for the whole attempt, enforces the hard ceiling (SIGTERM, `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`, SIGKILL) on its own clock and publishes `gate-exit.json` once the domain is empty. `fgos internal gate`; same crate and spec as the supervisor. | [run-supervisor/spec.md](run-supervisor/spec.md#5-supervisor-and-gate) |
| Agent protocol (L3) | Pure per-CLI adapters (claude, codex, agy, pi, omp) that read what an agent CLI showed (capture tail, exit, outbox) and name the result (`completed`, `blocked(login\|trust-dialog\|usage-limit)`, `needs-human`, `exited`); decide stdin policy and the activity source for idle. Never builds argv (that stays with the executor configuration through `resolveExecutorCommand`), never retries, no dependency on terminal-control, locks or attempts. Direct and terminal adapters; the terminal ones read the pane through `AgentIo` (`screen`, `inspect`) wired by the supervisor to terminal-control. Crate `fgos-agent-protocol` (`packages/agent-protocol/rust`). | [agent-protocol/spec.md](agent-protocol/spec.md) |
| Agent Mailbox (L4, signed at G0 on 2026-10-20; implementation not started) | Single authority for "how a message from one agent session is placed into the context of the right live head of a CLI on this machine, with an honest delivery report, and never as the user's input": the envelope, the delivery state machine (`recorded`, `in-flight`, `offered`, `refused`), the registry of heads (name, per-process generation, process `Record`), the channel-protection policies, the peer frame, and the per-CLI hook payload shape and non-terminal wake channels (the Claude Code scoped socket, `codex queue`). Recipients are independently started interactive heads, never a runner Unit attempt, a subagent or a teammate. Owns one runtime-state record per project at the main checkout's `.fgos` (not event truth, never replayed, never pushed). First slice imports only `fgos-process`, `fgos-holder-lock`, `fgos-durable-file` and `fgos-identity`; its core crate `fgos-mailbox-core` depends on serde alone. Never owns writer identity (Session Identity), process liveness (Process Facts & Control), the main-checkout `.fgos` resolver (the host), pane access (Terminal-control), typing or screen reading (Agent protocol; a later part), hook installation (the setup installer), locks (Holder-lock), communication authorization or case budgets (coordination foundation), or steering a Unit attempt (the runner). Rust crates `fgos-mailbox-core` and `fgos-mailbox` (planned: `packages/mailbox/rust`). | [agent-mailbox/spec.md](agent-mailbox/spec.md) |

13.1 Pane herdr bị confine cho agent không phải claude: công thức, lịch sử, vì sao từng bị quên
selected.text:
1. `credentialStore: { use: <codex | pi | omp>, homeEnv: <CODEX_HOME | PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR>, files?: [...] }` trên invocation (cùng dạng `codex-cli-bwrap`; runner.md RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). Config viết trước field này (config toàn máy, project khác) vẫn khai `resourceBindings: [{ resource: 'private-home', target: { kind: 'env', name: <biến> } }]`; một hàm (`credentialStoreOf`) suy `credentialStore` từ đó, và nhánh suy này bị xoá khi các config ấy đã chuyển.
2. Login của account đến từ inventory toàn máy `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts.<id>.credentialSource` trong `~/.fgos/config.json` (RUL65b của `docs/specs/runner.md`): kind `codex-home` (`auth.json`) hoặc `home-files` (danh sách file tường minh, copy owner-only, fail closed) — driver `drivers/bwrap.mjs` copy vào private home trước khi spawn, theo `credentialStore.files` của invocation nếu có, không thì theo danh sách của account. **Luật chép (2026-10-19, thay luật "thiếu một file thì từ chối"):** file có mặt thì chép, file vắng thì bỏ qua, không file nào có mặt thì từ chối `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`); symlink treo hay trỏ ra ngoài home, file không thường, đường dẫn có `..` vẫn bị từ chối. Invocation không khai store thì không được chép gì dù account nào được lease (bài học `569f72d3b`), và `assessBwrap` từ chối policy không cấp `private-home` cho invocation đọc store. Account có thể khai `credentialSources` (một store cho mỗi CLI, key là `credentialStore.use` của invocation); request của Authority (`buildConfinementRequest`) chọn store theo khoá đó, và khoá không có store thì bị từ chối trước khi worker chạy (runner.md RUL80 (account trước, CLI sau: một login store cho mỗi CLI)). Không mount thư mục account thật, không bypass flag thay sandbox.
3. Trust của workspace ghi vào store trong private home (`herdr-round.mjs` `trustStorePaths`), dẫn xuất từ store account thật — store của chính account được lease (credential source mà Authority chuyển cho adapter qua `trustAccountSource`), không phải account mà env tĩnh của invocation chỉ tới (runner.md RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)); với codex, trust từng hook của `<cwd>/.codex/hooks.json` (`[hooks.state."<đường dẫn tuyệt đối>:<event>:<nhóm>:<handler>"] trusted_hash`, băm theo luật của codex, ghim bằng test) được gieo cùng lúc, chỉ vào config của private home (không bao giờ vào config thật của account; private home bị xoá sau dispatch nên không có bước gỡ) và chỉ khi gốc repo đã được người dùng tin; với claude, các MCP server do `<cwd>/.mcp.json` khai báo được duyệt riêng cho tiến trình worker bằng `--settings` (`enabledMcpjsonServers`, thêm vào args khi chuẩn bị worker invocation; không ghi file dùng chung), cũng chỉ khi gốc repo đã được tin; `fgos doctor` check `confined-pane-accounts` báo invocation confine nào đọc store mà account không có file nào của store đó (agent sẽ khởi động chưa đăng nhập), và ghi chú file vắng.

### Writer Resolution Rules

**Registry chỉ ĐỐI CHIẾU, không bao giờ tự cấp danh tính** (per str46-io-contract): giá trị `id` lấy từ biến môi trường luôn giữ nguyên bất
kể sổ đăng ký có khớp hay không — sổ đăng ký chỉ nâng độ tin (`source`) khi
khớp, không bao giờ đổi hay tạo ra `id`. Một dòng sổ đăng ký KHÔNG BAO GIỜ
khớp theo thư mục làm việc hay theo pid của chính dòng đó — chỉ khớp đúng
`id` với `sessionId` của dòng — vì khớp theo thư mục sẽ gộp hai phiên khác
nhau trong cùng một worktree thành một danh tính, phá đúng mục đích khoá
hoạt động cây chính (xem spec Runner "Khoá hoạt động cây chính").

Một giá trị `id` sai định dạng (ký tự lạ, quá dài) bị LOẠI ở tầng phân giải
và rơi xuống nguồn kế tiếp — KHÔNG BAO GIỜ ném lỗi, KHÔNG BAO GIỜ chặn verb
(per str46-io-contract); không có validator nào đứng trên đường ghi
`writer`. `writer` fold lên item KHÔNG ĐIỀU KIỆN, GHI ĐÈ mỗi lần (latest-wins)
— khác khuôn "cộng thêm không đè" của outcome/friction/settlement, vì đây là
danh tính của LẦN GHI GẦN NHẤT, không phải một chuỗi lịch sử cần giữ mọi lần.
Item chưa từng qua tính năng này không mang `writer` — vắng mặt hoàn toàn,
tương thích ngược (RUL11 (tiến hóa schema)). Cơ chế phân giải đầy đủ (thứ tự nguồn, khoá hoạt động cây chính dùng cùng danh tính này): spec Runner RUL49 (compound-learning đổi trục: từ stage sang status retrospective).

  tiên: `registry` (đối chiếu được với `.fgos/sessions.json`, tin nhất) ·
  `env` (biến môi trường, ai cũng set được) · `pid` (tổ tiên cao nhất còn
  terminal, không có thì session id của tiến trình gọi; best-effort) ·
  `unresolved` (không nguồn nào xác nhận được — `id` vẫn là
  pid của chính tiến trình gọi, KHÔNG rỗng, KHÔNG vắng khoá; chỉ nhãn
  `source` nói giá trị chưa kiểm chứng được). Luật đầy đủ (thứ tự biến env,
  giới hạn đã biết) chỉ nằm ở [spec Session Identity](platform/identity/spec.md);
  nguồn duy nhất là crate Rust `fgos-identity`.

next.text: **Writer id của một lần chạy agent (attempt).** Một agent do `fgos run` khởi động ghi dưới id riêng của attempt đó, không phải id của controller đã khởi động nó: `writer.id` = `att-<attemptId>`, tính xác định từ attempt id (một resume ra đúng id cũ). Id được đặt vào `FGOS_SESSION_ID` của agent ở cả hai cách khởi động (headless và pane); biến `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` và `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` của cha bị gỡ trước khi agent chạy, và `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` được đặt lại bằng writer id của controller để lần theo dòng dõi (agent này do lần chạy nào sinh ra). Với `source` thì id đi theo luật env thường (`env` hoặc `registry`). Giới hạn đã biết: lệnh do codex chạy dưới daemon dùng chung chỉ thấy id của attempt khi codex được khởi động có tuỳ chọn `shell_environment_policy.set` (adapter pane tự thêm); nếu không, lệnh đó ghi dưới `CODEX_THREAD_ID`. Chi tiết: [spec Session Identity §5a và giới hạn](platform/identity/spec.md), cách đặt: [spec Run Supervisor](platform/run-supervisor/spec.md).
